purpose: Runtime ground-truth knowledge for the VITA chatbot.

poses.name: Goddess Pose
poses.description: A wide-legged standing squat with the feet turned outward, knees tracking in the direction of the toes, and the torso upright.
steps: Stand with the feet comfortably wide apart.
Turn both feet outward to a comfortable angle.
Bend the knees and lower the hips while keeping the knees tracking with the toes.
Keep the torso upright and the spine comfortable.
Place the hands at the chest or extend the arms comfortably.
Breathe steadily, then straighten the legs slowly to release.
poses.breathing: Breathe slowly and continuously. Do not hold the breath.
benefits: Develops body awareness and controlled posture.
beginner_modifications: Use stable support if balance is difficult.
precautions: Stop if the pose causes pain.
Do not force the knees or squat depth.
Seek qualified professional guidance for persistent or significant pain.
poses.suggested_hold: Start with about 10–20 seconds and gradually increase if comfortable.

poses.name: Downward-Facing Dog
poses.description: An inverted V-shaped posture in which the hands and feet support the body while the hips move up and back.
steps: Start on your hands and knees.
Spread the fingers and place the hands approximately shoulder-width apart.
Tuck the toes and lift the knees.
Send the hips up and back while lengthening the spine.
Keep the knees slightly bent if needed to maintain a comfortable spine.
Press through the hands and keep the head and neck relaxed.
Breathe steadily and lower the knees to release.
poses.breathing: Maintain slow, steady breathing and avoid holding the breath.
benefits: Strengthens and engages the arms and legs.
Lengthens the spine and the back of the body.
common_mistakes: Forcing the heels toward the floor.
beginner_modifications: Focus on a comfortable spine rather than forcing straight legs or heels to the floor.
precautions: Stop if you experience pain, dizziness, or unusual discomfort.
Do not force the heels to touch the floor.
Seek qualified professional guidance for persistent wrist, shoulder, or other significant pain.
poses.suggested_hold: Start with about 10–20 seconds or several comfortable breaths.

poses.name: Warrior II
poses.description: A standing posture with a wide stance, one knee bent, the opposite leg extended, and the arms reaching in opposite directions.
steps: Stand in a wide stance facing the long side of the mat.
Turn the front foot outward and angle the back foot slightly inward.
Bend the front knee while keeping it aligned over the ankle.
Extend both arms at approximately shoulder height in opposite directions.
Keep the torso upright and the shoulders relaxed.
Gaze toward the front hand if comfortable.
Hold for several steady breaths, then straighten the front leg and switch sides.
poses.breathing: Breathe steadily and continuously while holding the posture.
common_mistakes: Letting the front knee collapse inward.
Forcing an excessively deep knee bend.
Leaning the torso forward or backward.
beginner_modifications: Prioritize stable feet and an upright torso.
precautions: Stop if the posture causes pain.
Do not force the depth of the front knee bend.
Seek qualified professional guidance for persistent or significant hip or knee pain.
poses.suggested_hold: Start with about 15–30 seconds per side or several comfortable breaths.

poses.name: Plank Pose
poses.description: A strong bodyweight posture performed with the hands supporting the upper body and the legs extended, maintaining a stable body line.
steps: Start on your hands and knees.
Step the feet back one at a time.
Align the shoulders over or close to the wrists.
Create a long line from the shoulders through the hips toward the ankles.
Press firmly through the hands and keep the legs active.
Gently engage the abdomen while maintaining steady breathing.
Lower the knees or return to a comfortable position to release.
poses.breathing: Keep breathing steadily. Avoid holding the breath.
benefits: Engages the arms, shoulders, abdomen, hips, and legs.
beginner_modifications: Practice with the knees on the floor.
Focus on maintaining a stable body line rather than maximizing duration.
precautions: Stop if the pose causes pain.
Do not force a long hold when form is deteriorating.
Seek qualified professional guidance for persistent or significant wrist or shoulder pain.
poses.suggested_hold: Start with about 10–20 seconds and increase gradually if good form and steady breathing can be maintained.

poses.name: Tree Pose
poses.description: A standing balance posture in which one leg supports the body while the other foot rests against the inner standing leg above or below the knee.
steps: Stand upright with both feet grounded.
Shift your weight onto one leg.
Place the other foot against the inner standing leg either above or below the knee, not directly on the knee joint.
Keep the pelvis level and the standing leg stable.
Look at a steady point ahead.
Bring the hands to the chest or raise them overhead if comfortable.
Hold for several breaths, then lower the foot and switch sides.
poses.breathing: Breathe slowly and continuously while maintaining a steady gaze.
benefits: Improves body awareness and controlled posture.
common_mistakes: Placing the lifted foot directly on the standing knee.
Trying to balance without using available support when needed.
beginner_modifications: Keep the lifted toes on the floor with the heel near the opposite ankle.
Practice near a wall for support.
Use a steady gaze and progress gradually.
precautions: Step down safely if balance is lost.
Do not place the lifted foot directly on the standing knee.
Stop if the posture causes pain or unusual discomfort.
poses.suggested_hold: Start with about 10–20 seconds or several comfortable breaths per side.
